# CareerForge AI — Data Needed From Team

> **Last updated:** 2026-09-28  
> **Purpose:** Items the team must prepare by hand. The AI agent will draft templates and initial data; the team **must verify** before use.

---

## 1. Company Knowledge Base (Company DNA)

**What:** 30–50 target companies with real, public information about their hiring rounds.

**Format:** JSON (template will be generated by the agent in Phase 9)

**For each company, you need:**
| Field | Description | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Company name | Official name | — |
| Industry | IT Services, Product, Startup, etc. | — |
| Typical roles hired | SDE, Analyst, Consultant, etc. | Placement records |
| Eligibility | CGPA cut-off, branch restrictions, backlogs | Placement cell |
| Recruitment process | Number of rounds, order | Placement records, seniors |
| Round details | For each round: type, format, duration, topics, difficulty | Seniors, placement records |
| Tips | What worked for students who got selected | Verified student experiences |
| Package range | CTC range (LPA) | Public knowledge |
| Source | Where this info came from | Must be documented |
| Confidence | high / medium / low | Based on source quality |
| Last verified | Date someone checked this was still accurate | — |

**Where to get this data:**
- Your college's placement cell records
- Company career pages
- Verified student experiences (seniors who sat for these companies)
- Public forums (GeeksforGeeks, LeetCode Discuss, AmbitionBox) — mark confidence as "medium"

**⚠️ Important:** The agent will create a draft with generic data. You MUST verify every row before it goes into the app. Unverified data must be clearly marked.

**Deadline:** Before Phase 9 starts (approximately Week 4–5)

---

## 2. Seed Question Bank

**What:** Initial set of questions for aptitude, technical, and HR practice modules.

### Aptitude (~100 questions)
- Quantitative: 30–40 (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, permutation, probability, time & work, etc.)
- Logical reasoning: 30–40 (patterns, puzzles, seating arrangement, blood relations, coding-decoding)
- Verbal: 20–30 (grammar, reading comprehension, vocabulary, para jumbles)

### Technical (~150 questions)
- DSA: 30 (arrays, strings, trees, graphs, DP, sorting, searching)
- DBMS: 20 (normalization, SQL queries, ER diagrams, transactions)
- OS: 20 (processes, threads, deadlocks, memory, scheduling)
- Computer Networks: 20 (OSI/TCP-IP, protocols, subnetting)
- OOP: 20 (concepts, design patterns, SOLID)
- SQL: 20 (queries, joins, aggregations, subqueries)
- Miscellaneous: 20 (system design basics, web fundamentals)

### HR (~50 questions)
- Behavioral: 25 (tell me about yourself, strengths/weaknesses, teamwork, leadership)
- Situational: 15 (conflict resolution, deadline pressure, failure handling)
- Company-specific: 10 (why this company, where do you see yourself)

**Format:** JSON with fields: question, type, difficulty, topic, options (for MCQ), correct_answer, explanation, source

**What the agent does:** Drafts initial questions + generates more with AI (verified by a solve pass)  
**What the team does:** Reviews, corrects, adds questions from actual placement experiences

**Deadline:** Before Phase 12 starts (approximately Week 5)

---

## 3. Sample Resumes for Evaluation (Phase 19)

**What:** 30–50 resumes for testing the resume parser and ATS scorer.

**Requirements:**
- Mix of formats: PDF (formatted), PDF (scanned), DOCX
- Mix of quality: excellent, average, poor
- Mix of branches: CS, IT, ECE, Mechanical, etc.
- Anonymized (remove real phone, email, address — use fake ones)
- With permission from the owner

**Where to get:**
- Your own resumes (different versions)
- Friends' resumes (with permission, anonymized)
- Create a few intentionally bad resumes for testing edge cases

**What you label for each resume:**
- Manually identify: name, email, education, skills, experience, projects
- Rate ATS-friendliness: 1–10
- Note any parsing challenges (tables, columns, images, fancy formatting)

**Deadline:** Before Phase 19 starts (approximately Week 9)

---

## 4. Human-Rated Mock Answers (Phase 19)

**What:** 30 mock interview answers scored by team members (for AI vs human agreement test)

**Process:**
1. Agent generates 30 interview questions (10 technical, 10 HR, 10 project-based)
2. Agent generates sample answers (varying quality: good, okay, poor)
3. Each team member independently scores each answer on the rubric (0–10 per dimension)
4. These human scores are compared with AI scores (Cohen's kappa)

**Rubric dimensions:**
- Correctness / Relevance
- Depth of explanation
- Structure / Clarity
- Communication quality
- Relevance to job role

**Deadline:** Before Phase 19 starts (approximately Week 9)

---

## 5. User Study Participants (Phase 19)

**What:** 20–30 classmates to test the app and fill a survey

**What they do:**
1. Create an account
2. Upload/build a resume
3. Select a target company
4. Go through at least one mock interview
5. Fill SUS (System Usability Scale) questionnaire
6. Optionally: compare their mock scores before and after using the roadmap

**What you need to prepare:**
- List of willing participants
- A Google Form for SUS + feedback
- Permission / consent form (if required by college)
- Schedule for testing sessions

**Deadline:** Week 9–10
